description: 9-5-2: trick-taking game; name may refer to card ranks or deal (e.g. 9, 5, 2 cards). Trump and follow suit; point or trick count to win. Played in India and elsewhere.

content.text: 9-5-2: trick-taking game; name may refer to card ranks or deal (e.g. 9, 5, 2 cards). Trump and follow suit; point or trick count to win. Played in India and elsewhere.
Related to Sergeant Major (RAF: 3p, 16 cards, targets 8-5-3). 9-5-2 and its close relative 3-2-5 (Teen Do Panch) are played in India, Pakistan and Nepal using a reduced pack with trick quotas.

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 6
Optimal Players: 4
Partnerships: Optional

Type: Standard 52-card deck
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included

Standard 52-card deck
Score sheet (optional)
Table space

Cards per Player: Varies by player count
Dealing Pattern: Clockwise

items.text: Clockwise Deal and Play: Deal and play can proceed clockwise instead of counter-clockwise, with the player to dealer's left taking the higher trick quota, choosing trumps, and leading to the first trick while the player to dealer's right takes the lower quota.

Sevens as Permanent Trumps: In some circles both Sevens are permanent trumps: the 7 of hearts is the highest trump, followed by the 7 of spades, then the remaining cards of the chosen trump suit in their usual order.
